Is there any very urgent matter - and perhaps I'll first address the representative of Bosnia-Herzegovina - that should be added? And before you -- if you would like to respond to what Mr. Yatvin said, perhaps I as the Presiding Judge of this Chamber can tell you that the structure of 11 bis is that either the Prosecution or this Bench proprio motu initiates the referral proceedings, and that this Chamber has never, ever experienced that Bosnia-Herzegovina, in whatever way, has implicitly or explicitly expressed in any way that they would rely on this Referral Bench to serve their interests. I want to be quite clear on that. Is there any further need, Ms. Popadic, to add something to the many things that have been said already?

utterances.speaker: MS. POPADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Indeed, I have nothing further to add, other than to say that, in view of everything that has been said here, that neither in this case or in any other case is there a single argument that would indicate that not all the standards had been met by Bosnia-Herzegovina to have this particular case tried before the state court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Popadic. Is -- would either the Ambassador of Argentina or you, Mr. Obradovic, would like to add something? Just to say that you don't have anything to add takes time from the last two or three minutes of our tape. So if there's nothing to be added, that's understood. If there is anything urgent to be added, apart perhaps you asked an opportunity to make further submissions; if possible within a week, that would be highly appreciated by this Chamber. Anything further?

utterances.speaker: MR. GONI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just to request, I'm sure this will take place in any case, but a very careful translation of a very clear and precise statement on the part of my government may be -- and if it may be distributed to all the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The written translation is prepared and will be filed in the case file of this case. Yes, Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, finally I would like to emphasise that the Republic of Serbia is fully prepared to give a written submission on any matters concerning the referral of this case to our state, should the Referral Bench find it necessary. Thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we need it, we'll ask for it. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a point in response to Mr. Yatvin's comment that level or description as being in the generic terminology of Security Council resolutions has not been the dominant factor. In fact, this Chamber, this Bench, has referred generals, by level, seemingly out of the range but by virtue of referring to the indictment and understanding the context in which the allegations are made, the hierarchial issues, generals have been referred to national courts. Leaders such as Jankovic have been referred. The fact of commanding others has not been a determinative factor; there are a number of factors. Secondly, in terms of the Security Council resolutions which discuss what can be done by this Tribunal generally, we are charged with implementing the measures for completion, among them, of course, is the referral to national jurisdictions and the President of this Tribunal specifically required to implement measures, which includes all the rule-making process. So the fact that an accused may be out in the field somewhere in the world and is brought before this Tribunal, which must happen by virtue of Article 29, poses no limitation on what happens once they get here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. Any further submissions to be made by you, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Your Honour, if you will allow me just to say a small correction. There are two cases against Milan Lukic before the Serbian justice system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The first one is a Cvjevarin [phoen]. He is sentenced for 20 years' prison. And the case number two is the case Strpci [phoen], which is case number 1 before the Special Court for War Crimes, and they started investigation about that incident. My learned friend, Mr. Knezevic, can tell more -- much more details, but I know -- I understand the time limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is another case pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just to support my learned friend, Mr. Yatvin. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Yatvin, we've got one minute left on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to say that I hope that my excess hyperbole did not offend the Bench. The point I was making is that the state of Bosnia did not go to Argentina as Serbia did, perhaps relying on this procedure. And I meant no assumption of what the response --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Yatvin, any other words pending on it would again draw the attention which was at least an unfortunate phrasing of your thoughts.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Lukic and Mr. Lukic, it was a very technical hearing. I hope you have understood everything. It's of a legal, technical nature. The Chamber will adjourn, and when there's any additional information needed, we'll ask for it. We stand adjourned sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: sine die at 4.22 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Rule 11 bis hearing adjourned
